svg.text: Virtually indexed, physically tagged · 4 ways × 16 sets × 32 B line (parameterised) · write-back, write-allocate · 3-cycle access
REQUEST — shared between the LSU and the page-table walker (RXVDCacheArb: walker has priority)
CYCLE 1 — RAM read, indexed with the virtual address
CYCLE 2 — tag compare against the physical address, RAM write on a hit
miss : busy until the fill completes
device: busy until the bus replies
the LSU kills and replays newer uops
byte-enable write into DataRam[hit_way][offset] in cycle 2 — no write buffer,
no allocate-on-write-miss stall; DirtyRam[hit_way] is set at the same time
device writes never update the RAMs
rotate + sign extend in the LSU
replay the access as a hit
a miss blocks the cache: no hit under miss, no write buffer, no MSHR
FILL 8 beats read into DataRam[victim way]; the tag is written on the last beat
FLUSH 8 beats writing the dirty victim back before the fill starts
CLEAN sweeps every dirty line out to memory, then RUN resumes
UNCACHED device reads and writes bypass the RAMs completely and are
never cached, so the LSU sees them as variable-latency accesses
